brief: GS flags sentiment at an extreme: its Vol Panic Index closed Friday at 9.8/10, a level that historically has marked a good entry point for adding risk, with two caveats this time, the Fed is hiking rather than cutting, and hedge funds are aggressively adding shorts. The semis drawdown is now cycle-sized: the SOX is down ~43% from its June 2026 peak, beyond a typical mid-cycle correction and in line with prior severe downturns, the fourth-largest SOX drawdown since 1999. This is still a de-rating, not yet an earnings downturn, though GIR cut its 2028 memory pricing forecasts over the weekend while keeping its constructive 2027 undersupply view, cutting Samsung and SK Hynix price targets while keeping both rated Buy. Credit markets show AI-chip financing tightening, SpaceX's SPV/lease deal priced above 8%, and neocloud credit spreads and yields remain stressed. GS Prime Brokerage data show hedge funds net selling for a third straight week, record shorting activity, and CTA models forecasting further selling into next week. Separately, the note flags an Amazon Buy reiteration, a Worldline cash-flow controversy, and a reported CrowdStrike-Zscaler takeover approach.
